title: Naval 专题 · AI 时代的 Naval：回到写代码
title_en: Naval Series · Naval in the Age of AI: Back to Code

questions.question: 按这篇的梳理，Naval 认为代码人人都能写之后，价值主要转到了哪里？
options: 掌握最新的提示词技巧，以及别人包装好的工作流框架
能做出别人不会做的酷软件，并抢先发布出去
懂底层的知识、选对题的判断、为结果背书的担责
雇更多工程师，组建更大的软件团队来扩大规模
questions.explanation: 他给过三个答案：抽象会漏，懂底层的人才能补漏；选对题和选错题差的是无穷大；人正在变成验证者，为 AI 的产出背书。他明确说「我在做别人不会做的酷软件」不值得投资，也说自己不学提示词技巧。
questions.question_en: Per this overview, once anyone can write code, where does Naval think the value mainly shifts?
options_en: Mastering the latest prompt tricks and other people's packaged workflow frameworks
Building cool software others can't build, and shipping it before anyone else
Knowing the layer below, judgment in picking problems, and accountability for results
Hiring more engineers and building bigger software teams to scale up
questions.explanation_en: He gives three answers: abstractions leak and those who understand the layer below can patch them; picking the right problem versus the wrong one is an infinite difference; and people are becoming verifiers who vouch for AI output. He explicitly calls 'I build cool software others can't' uninvestable and says he doesn't learn prompt tricks.

questions.question: Naval 说自己不学任何提示词技巧和工作流框架。这篇文章怎么看这句话？
options: 这证明模型已经足够聪明了，完全不懂工程的人也能得到一模一样的产出
这说明他完全放弃了工作流，只靠一次次随手的单轮对话
这是因为让几个模型互相审代码，已足以弥补技巧上的不足
有前提：他懂计算机架构，能把需求讲精确，不学的只是包装好的技巧
questions.explanation: 文章指出他能用结构化英语把需求讲精确，是因为懂计算机架构；他搭的提交即审查、每天自动修 bug 本身就是讲究的工作流。他不学的是别人包装好的技巧，不是工程常识。他还观察到模型互审有严重的群体思维，并不管用。
questions.question_en: Naval says he doesn't learn any prompting techniques or workflow frameworks. How does the article read that claim?
options_en: It proves models are now smart enough that non-engineers get the same output
It shows he has abandoned workflows entirely and relies on casual one-off prompts
It's because having several models review each other's code makes up for missing technique
It has a premise: he knows computer architecture and can specify precisely; he skips only packaged tricks
questions.explanation_en: The article notes he can specify needs precisely in structured English because he understands computer architecture, and his setup — automatic review on commit, daily automated bug fixing — is itself a careful workflow. What he skips is other people's packaged tricks, not engineering sense. He also found that models reviewing each other suffer heavy groupthink.

questions.question: Naval 把判断 AI 能否创造的标准，从「追问它为什么」换成了「分布外」。文章对这个新标准提出了什么批评？
options: 分布外是机器学习术语，不能拿来讨论人类意义上的创造
这个新标准和 Deutsch 关于人是普遍解释者的理论直接相互矛盾
这个标准太宽松，让 AI 很容易就被认定为具有了创造力
照此定义，AI 每学会一样东西，那样东西就自动不算创造，难以证伪
questions.explanation: 吉卜力画风的讨论暴露了问题：一种风格被 AI 铺天盖地复制之后就进了分布，不再算艺术。这样 AI 每学会一样，那样就不算创造了，和他要求别人做「有风险、可证伪的预测」恰好相反。
questions.question_en: Naval switched his test for whether AI can create from 'ask it why' to 'out of distribution'. What criticism does the article raise about the new test?
options_en: 'Out of distribution' is a machine-learning term and can't apply to human creativity
The test directly contradicts Deutsch's theory of humans as universal explainers
The test is too loose, making it easy to declare that AI has become creative
By that definition, whatever AI learns automatically stops counting as creation, making it unfalsifiable
questions.explanation_en: The Ghibli-style discussion exposed it: once AI floods the world with a style, it's in distribution and no longer counts as art. So each thing AI learns stops counting as creation — the opposite of the risky, falsifiable predictions he demands of others.
